# ios stack pack: standards

Scope: iOS apps in Swift and SwiftUI, with the project generated by XcodeGen.

Globs: `**/*.swift`, `**/project.yml`

Apply these standards only to files that match the globs. Project docs win over this pack. This pack wins over principles. A standard that overrides a principle names it.

## 1. project.yml is the source of the Xcode project

**Rule:** Change targets, settings, files, and versions in `project.yml`. Then run `xcodegen generate`. Do not edit `*.xcodeproj` by hand.

**Why:** `xcodegen generate` writes the `.xcodeproj` again from `project.yml`. A hand edit to the `.xcodeproj` is lost on the next run.

**Violation:** The diff changes `project.pbxproj` with no matching change in `project.yml`. Or a new Swift file is outside every `sources` path of `project.yml`.

## 2. Layers by folder

**Rule:** Put pure value types and decision logic in `Domain/`. Put protocols for services in `Domain/Services/`. Put concrete services (API, Keychain, store, audio, speech) in `Infrastructure/`. Put each feature in `Features/<Feature>/` with its view and view model. Put shared views in `Shared/`. Put the app entry, wiring, and navigation in `App/`.

**Why:** A reader finds a feature in one folder. Domain code stays free of frameworks, so it is testable with plain structs.

**Violation:** A file in `Domain/` imports SwiftUI, SwiftData, GRDB, or `URLSession`. A view or view model sits outside `Features/` and is used by one feature only.

## 3. Decision logic is pure Domain code

**Rule:** Put each rule, mapping, derivation, and plan in a pure function or a value type in `Domain/`. The view model and the services execute the result. They do not branch on business rules.

**Why:** The riskiest logic (sync, conflicts, conversion, eligibility) is then testable without mocks. Mock-heavy async tests of view models give low signal.

**Violation:** A new `if` or `switch` on a domain state in a view model or a service. A DTO-to-domain mapping inside a view model. A test of a rule that needs a protocol mock.

## 4. Domain models are Sendable value types

**Rule:** Model domain concepts as `struct` and `enum` types that are `Sendable`, and `Codable` when they cross a boundary. Use `let` properties. A change returns a new value from a method on the type or a pure function.

**Why:** Value types copy on assignment, so no other code changes a value under you. They cross actors without data races.

**Violation:** A `class` in `Domain/Models/`. A `var` property on a domain struct that callers set from outside. A domain type marked `@unchecked Sendable`.

**Overrides:** `principle-rich-domain-model`. The app has no mutable entity with identity in memory. The rules live on the immutable value type or in a pure function, not on a reference type with private setters.

## 5. Persistence types stay in Infrastructure

**Rule:** Keep store records (SwiftData `@Model`, GRDB records) and their mapping in `Infrastructure/`. Domain types do not import the store or carry its attributes.

**Why:** A store framework then changes without a change to the domain. Domain tests need no database.

**Violation:** `import SwiftData` or `import GRDB` in `Domain/`. A view model reads a `@Model` type directly where a domain type exists.

## 6. One enum for async state

**Rule:** Model each async load with the project `LoadingState<T>` enum: `.idle`, `.loading`, `.loaded(T)`, `.failed(Error)`. Switch on it in the view.

**Why:** One enum makes the invalid mixes impossible, for example "loading and failed at the same time".

**Violation:** A view model with two or more of `isLoading`, `error`, and an optional result that must stay in sync.

## 7. @Observable view models on the main actor

**Rule:** Mark each view model `@MainActor @Observable final class`. Do not use `ObservableObject`, `@Published`, or `@StateObject` in new code.

**Why:** `@Observable` tracks only the properties that a view reads, so a view updates less. `@MainActor` makes UI state changes safe at compile time.

**Violation:** `ObservableObject` or `@Published` in the diff. A view model with no `@MainActor`. `DispatchQueue.main.async` to set view state.

## 8. Wiring through one dependency container

**Rule:** Construct services in the `Dependencies` container and inject it through the SwiftUI environment. Put each service behind a protocol. The container only constructs and holds services.

**Why:** Tests swap a protocol for a fake at one seam. A container that holds logic grows into a second, untested domain.

**Violation:** A view or view model constructs a concrete service. A new method with branching logic on `Dependencies`. A singleton (`static let shared`) for a new service.

## 9. Derive view state once, off the main actor

**Rule:** Derive expensive view data once into an immutable `Sendable` snapshot, off the main actor. Views read stored fields. Use `LazyVStack` or `List` for long scroll content. Do not allocate a `DateFormatter` or a similar formatter in a loop or in `body`.

**Why:** A computed property on an `@Observable` view model runs again on each body update, also during scroll. That gives visible jitter.

**Violation:** A computed property on a view model that scans a collection. A `ScrollView { VStack { ForEach ... } }` over unbounded data. `DateFormatter()` inside `body`, `ForEach`, or a `map`.

## 10. Credentials only in the Keychain

**Rule:** Store tokens, passwords, and server connections only in the Keychain. Do not store them in `UserDefaults`, files, SwiftData, GRDB, or next to other cached data. Read a token live when you need it.

**Why:** Other stores are not encrypted with the device key and can go into backups. A token copied into a cache outlives sign-out.

**Violation:** A key with `token`, `password`, or `secret` in a `UserDefaults` call. A token field on a persisted record or a cache file.

## 11. No secrets in logs or in error text

**Rule:** Do not use `print()` in app code. Log through `os.Logger` or the project log facade, with privacy markers. Never log tokens, auth headers, or request and response bodies. Show the user a fixed error message. Do not put `error.localizedDescription` in UI text.

**Why:** Logs ship in Release builds and in diagnostic exports. A system error text can hold host names, paths, and URLs with tokens.

**Violation:** `print(` in a non-test file. A log call that interpolates a URL, a header, or a body without redaction. `Text("... \(error.localizedDescription)")`.

## 12. Stable accessibility identifiers on controls

**Rule:** Give each control that a UI test or a verification drive taps an `accessibilityIdentifier` in the form `<screen>_<element>`. Give each icon-only button an accessibility label.

**Why:** UI tests and verification drives find elements by identifier. A label changes with copy edits and localization. Coordinates break on each layout change.

**Violation:** A new button, field, or row that a test reaches by its visible text or by coordinates. An `Image` button with no `accessibilityLabel`.

## 13. Swift Testing for unit tests, XCUITest for UI

**Rule:** Write unit tests with Swift Testing (`import Testing`, `@Test`, `#expect`). Build test data with fixture builders. Write UI tests with XCUITest. Test pure Domain code directly, with no mocks.

**Why:** Swift Testing gives parameterized tests and clear failure output. Pure code needs no fake to test.

**Violation:** A new `XCTestCase` for a unit test. A Domain test that injects a mock. A UI test that drives a view model directly.

## 14. Pin the simulator by UDID

**Rule:** Run tests on a simulator that the run creates, and address it with `-destination "id=<udid>"`. Delete it at the end. Use the project test scripts when they exist.

**Why:** Many simulators can share a name across iOS runtimes. Then `xcodebuild` stops and waits for input. Two worktrees on one simulator corrupt each other.

**Violation:** `-destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16'` in a script, a doc, or a CI file. A script that boots a simulator and has no cleanup trap.
